theory.text: The most common rookie mistake in vibe coding: stuffing an entire product into a single prompt. 'Build me an e-commerce app with login, cart, payments, admin, and mobile support.' The AI will produce something. It will look impressive. It will also be a mess that's almost impossible to debug.
Big ambitions, small prompts. Pick one thin slice — a single feature, a single screen — and ship it. Then move to the next. Each commit is a save point you can fall back to when something breaks.

bad.label: One mega-prompt
bad.content: Build a full to-do app with login, dark mode, categories, sharing, and Google Calendar sync.

good.label: Slice by slice
good.content: 1. Homepage with empty list. 2. Add + complete tasks. 3. Group by category. 4. Show counter at top.

theory.text: If a single prompt could break your project, you're prompting too big. Cut it in half. Then in half again.

exercise.prompt_template: Build complex things by working in [BLANK] steps, shipping [BLANK] feature at a time.

blanks.hint_2: Each step should be small enough to verify in a minute or two.
blanks.explanation: The answer is 'small' (or 'tiny'). Small steps mean small bugs. Big steps mean tangled bugs you can't unwind.

blanks.hint_1: How many features should you tackle in one prompt?
blanks.hint_2: Just enough to build, test, and commit before moving on.
blanks.explanation: The answer is 'one'. One feature per prompt, one commit per feature. That rhythm keeps you in control.

outro.recap: You learned the small-step principle. Slice the work, ship one piece, commit, repeat.
outro.next_prompt: Next: why context matters more than the prompt itself.
